finding.claim: GET /users returns id and name for any org chosen by the caller, with no authentication or authorization check (broken access control / cross-tenant disclosure).
finding.source: req.query.org, supplied by any unauthenticated HTTP client via GET /users?org=... (db.js:9).
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, serialized back via res.json (db.js:9-10).

trace.note: app.get('/users') async handler; no identity or membership check.
org taken from req.query.org and bound as $1 to the query.
all returned rows sent to the client via res.json.

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query prevents SQL injection. No authn/authz middleware in this file. Caveat: if upstream middleware enforces auth and scopes org, this is out of scope; none is visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers app.get("/users") with no auth or org-membership middleware. db.js:9 binds req.query.org directly as $1, which blocks SQL injection but not cross-tenant selection. db.js:10 returns all rows via res.json. The only other file is none (Glob shows db.js alone), and db.js:23 calls app.listen on this same app, so no upstream router sits in front of this route.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can call GET /users?org=X at db.js:9 and receive every id and name for that org via res.json at db.js:10, with no authn/authz check anywhere in db.js:8-10 or in the single-file app that listens at db.js:23. Caveat: req.pg is never set in this repo, so as written the handler would throw at db.js:9 unless a pg middleware is attached elsewhere; that does not block the access-control flaw once it is wired up.

finding.claim: Any unauthenticated request to /users throws a TypeError because req.pg is never assigned in this file; the async handler's rejection is not caught by Express 4, so the request hangs or the process crashes on Node 15+.
finding.sink: req.pg.query at db.js:9 with req.pg undefined (availability / unhandled rejection).

trace.note: req.pg read; undefined unless upstream middleware sets it, so .query throws.
app.listen(3002) exposes the route to the network.

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch, no error middleware, no assignment of req.pg anywhere in the repo. Conditional: only if no upstream middleware sets req.pg. Express version unknown (no package.json); on Express 5 the rejection goes to the error handler and does not crash.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only file in the repo is db.js. The route at db.js:8 has no auth middleware, no try/catch, and no error handler. A grep for req.pg, .pg=, and pg= finds only the read at db.js:9. Nothing assigns req.pg. The app.listen(3002) at db.js:23 binds with no host argument, so the route is network-reachable.
verdict.reason: Anonymous GET /users reaches `req.pg.query` at db.js:9 with `req.pg` never assigned (the grep finds no assignment in the repo), so it throws a TypeError. Express 4 does not catch the rejected promise from the async handler at db.js:8, so the request hangs and, on Node 15+, the unhandled rejection can crash the process. The crash is version-dependent: on Express 5 the rejection goes to the error handler and returns a 500 without crashing. The request-level TypeError is certain; the process-crash impact needs Express 4, which cannot be confirmed without a package.json.
